function: Check whether the directed graph has a unique topological ordering
implementation_type: Adjacency list + recursive DFS + stack for topological sorting; then checks whether every consecutive pair in the topological order has a direct edge
notes: Uses recursive DFS in topsort(), marks visited nodes and pushes each node onto a stack after visiting its neighbours, which is the standard DFS-based topological sort. After obtaining the ordering, it checks every consecutive pair of vertices for a direct edge. In a DAG, this is used to determine whether the topological ordering is unique. The unordered_set is used to find a possible zero-indegree starting vertex.

function: Check whether the directed graph has a unique topological ordering
implementation_type: Adjacency list + indegree array + FIFO queue; uniqueness is checked by requiring exactly one zero-indegree vertex to be available at every step
notes: Computes the indegree of every vertex, inserts all zero-indegree vertices into a queue, and repeatedly removes one vertex while decreasing the indegrees of its neighbours. A neighbour is added when its indegree becomes zero. If the queue contains more than one vertex at any stage, there are multiple possible topological orders, so the solution outputs 0. Otherwise it outputs 1. This is Kahn's topological sorting algorithm with a uniqueness check.

implementation_type: Adjacency list + indegree array + LIFO stack for zero-indegree vertices + consecutive-edge uniqueness check
notes: Computes the indegree of every vertex and repeatedly removes a zero-indegree vertex, decreasing the indegrees of its neighbours and adding newly zero-indegree vertices to a stack. This is an indegree-based Kahn topological sort, using a LIFO stack instead of a FIFO queue. After building one topological ordering, it checks whether every pair of consecutive vertices has a direct edge; this is used to determine whether the topological ordering is unique.
